request.state: The user wants the smallest complete Can language installation, one command without manually installing runtimes. Verified: compiler release is 2.2MiB. Platform JS requires Node>=22 (Node24 verified). Four bundle paths invoke Bun including generated view entries whose source depends on user apps. workerd darwin-arm64 is109MiB. Native preparation helper is593KiB. Browser automation is optional for preview but mandatory for generation acceptance with authored Playwright tests. Current producer files use import.meta.url, dynamic loading, WASM and manifests. No clean installed Bun-runtime compatibility evidence exists. Existing build tool esbuild is a dev dependency; replacing runtime Bun builds changes emitted JS and needs qualification. We can ship a production-only closure plus matching private Node and Bun without changing engine behavior, measure it, then optimize demonstrated large costs. Alternatively replace Bun bundling with esbuild and qualify all affected output semantics, or use Bun for Node code and qualify IPC/runtime compatibility. Compare these as next implementation steps, not permanent ideals.

approach.instructions: Which immediate implementation step best balances a complete no-prerequisite install, measured size and preservation of current workflows?

criteria.preserve: Ship only production closure with matching private Node and Bun; retain algorithms, measure bytes, defer unproven engine changes.
criteria.esbuild: Replace Bun runtime bundling with esbuild and validate changed generated output before shipping.
criteria.bun_only: Run host JS under Bun as well as its bundler and validate Node compatibility and process behavior.
